maya: Heads-up — I'm sketching a proposal for a "graceful fallthrough" admission approach when orgs/keys hit capacity-driven rate limits. Want quick feedback before I formalize it. :thinking:

maya: Problem: when a GPU pool saturates we currently hard-429 or queue unbounded. Customers see sudden errors or long tails. We need smoother degradation tied to capacity and org-level importance (paid vs free).

maya: Proposal (high-level):
- Per-org "grace credits" that let requests slip through during short bursts based on recent usage and SLA tier.
- A small bounded spillover queue at the front proxy that holds requests for up to ~250-500ms while we attempt to route to nearby headroom (regional or lower-cost model).
- Soft-429 with structured metadata for clients: `Retry-After`, `X-Redwood-Mode` (e.g., reduced-precision, smaller-model), and a priority-token header.

maya: Rough config idea:
```
# per-org token bucket blended with capacity weight
org.rate_limit: 200 req/s
org.burst: 400
org.grace_credits: 30  # allows N extra tokens per minute for short bursts
pool.capacity_score: 1.0  # normalized pool headroom
spillover.window_ms: 300
spillover.max_queue: 200
```

maya: Behavior: when pool reports saturation, admission controller drains from the org token bucket first. If token bucket exhausted but org has grace_credits, allow requests to enter short spillover queue and decrement a credit. If queue exceeds window or credits exhausted, return soft-429.

raj: I like the grace credit idea. Two quick Qs: how do we refill credits? time-based or consumption-based? and how do we avoid credit gaming (clients intentionally bursting small calls)?

maya: refill is time-based with a decay that tracks recent sustained usage — refill slowly if steady high throughput. We can also tie refill rate to payment tier (enterprise gets faster refill). For gaming we can require credits to be consumed only when actual GPU allocation succeeded previously (i.e., credits earned by successful under-capacity requests).

olivia: From SRE POV we need a clear signal for backpressure propagation to downstream services (esp. integrators). Can we add a header/trailer that indicates the pool id + current headroom percentage so SDKs can adjust client-side batching? e.g., `X-Redwood-Pool-Headroom: 0.12`

sam: SDKs can do client-side smoothing if they get that. Also want to make sure regional constraints respected — if we route to another region for headroom we must ensure data residency rules. Maybe spillover routing should be constrained per org flag: `allow_cross_region_fallback: true|false`.

maya: Agreed. We'll default to no cross-region fallback for orgs with private deployments or strict residency. For hosted customers we can have opt-in. We'll make it explicit in the soft-429 payload.

raj: Cost note: if we route from a cheaper model to a larger one as fallback that increases cost. I think prefer routing to smaller / quantized variants first (same model family) before moving to higher-cost options. Also track cost uplift per-org and expose as usage line item.

maya: yep — ordered fallback policy: 1) same model quantized variant, 2) smaller-capacity model variant, 3) cross-region if allowed, 4) reserved burst (paid-only). Each step annotated in response metadata.

olivia: For metrics we'll need:
- per-org allowed/blocked counts
- grace credits consumed/refilled
- average spillover queue latency
- fallback step distribution
- per-pool headroom over time
These are critical for debugging and incident playbooks.

sam: Implementation thoughts: admission should be colocated with the edge proxy (low-latency) to make quick decisions. Pull periodic pool-level telemetry from control plane (~1s granularity) and maintain an in-memory capacity score. Use a small circuit-breaker so we don't thrash pool state on noisy telemetry.

maya: Good. Also want to avoid single-resource bookkeeping explosion. We'll do hierarchical token buckets: org -> key -> route. Credits can live at org level only to keep state small.

raj: Edge cases: what if an org exhausts credits and starts getting soft-429s, but then a low-priority org frees capacity quickly? We should allow emergency short replenishment if pool headroom jumps by >30% within 1s. That avoids leaving paying customers blocked unnecessarily.

maya: Add fast-path replenish if pool_headroom_delta > threshold. And a per-org cooldown so they don't oscillate.

infra-bot: deploy-check: admission-proxy v2.3.1 has a new spillover queue feature behind feature-flag `spillover_v2`. Canary target: eng-platform -> 5% of requests next deploy.

olivia: :thumbsup: let's start a small canary and collect the metrics above. Also add tracing tags `admission.reason` and `admission.fallback_step` for postmortem.

maya: I'll draft a short RFC with diagrams and config knobs. Link when ready — plan to iterate Wednesday. Thanks for quick takes. :rocket:

sam: one more: client guidance in SDKs — if they see `X-Redwood-Mode: reduced-precision` we should expose a simple retry-with-backoff helper that optionally downgrades prompt size or enables streaming to reduce token pressure.

raj: Agreed. Also add billing visibility for fallback cost to prevent surprises.

olivia: Sounds good. I'll add SLO checks to the runbook to ensure we don't silently hit error budgets during rollout.

maya: great — I'll post the RFC link here when it's up.

maya: thanks — closing for now.
